items.title: Topic Nine Opens: Who Crosses the Flood?

items.zh: 誰能越暴流？誰能超大海？誰能捨眾苦？誰能得清淨？
items.en: Who can cross the flood? Who can cross the great sea? Who can relinquish all suffering? Who can attain purity?

items.zh: 正信越暴流；無逸超大海；精進捨眾苦；智慧得清淨。
items.en: Right faith crosses the flood. Heedfulness crosses the great sea. Vigour relinquishes all suffering. Wisdom attains purity.

items.zh: 今此頌中，云何正信能越暴流？謂如有一，為欲了知諸欲過患，聽佛所說若弟子說所有正法。聞是法已，獲得正信，便生欲樂，為斷事欲及煩惱欲，遂能棄捨居家事欲，正信出家，往趣非家。既出家已，為欲斷除煩惱諸欲，遠離而住。彼由熾燃勤精進故，乃至修習正思惟故，斷煩惱諸欲，得離欲定地。如是正信為依為導，便能越度諸欲暴流。云何無逸能超大海？謂於彼定終不愛味，乃至亦無堅著安住；唯除為證諸漏盡智，專注其心。由此定心清淨、鮮白、正直、調柔，於四聖諦能入現觀，乃至證得諸漏永盡。如是由不放逸為依、為導，能斷色、無色繫二有暴流，及斷一切無明與見二種暴流，是故名為超渡大海。云何精進能捨眾苦？謂如有一，有學見迹，作是思惟：我應當證三界離欲，諸結永盡。便臻遠離，於彼勇猛精勤而住，不多安止貪欲纏心。又能如實了知現在諸欲貪纏所有出離，於貪欲蓋淨修其心，遂能斷滅諸貪欲纏，及貪欲纏為緣所生心諸憂苦。如貪欲蓋，乃至疑蓋，當知亦爾。如是精進為依、為導，能捨眾苦。云何智慧能得清淨？謂彼除滅能染污心，乃至能障究竟涅槃五種蓋已，即依未至安住未至。如先所得苦集滅道諸無漏智，於諸苦中思惟真苦，乃至於道思惟真道，便得無餘三界離欲，諸漏永盡。如是由先所得智慧為依、為導，能證清淨。復次，今當略辨上所說義。謂薄伽梵於此頌中，略顯異生先已離欲，後於聖諦現觀清淨；及顯有學於諸聖諦現觀為先，離欲清淨。當知是名此中略義。
items.en: In this verse, how does right faith cross the flood? Someone, wishing to understand the dangers of sense pleasures, listens to the true Dharma taught by the Buddha or by his disciples. Having heard this Dharma, they gain right faith and give rise to the wish to cut off desire for objects and desire as affliction. So they are able to give up the sense objects of household life and, with right faith, go forth from home into homelessness. Having gone forth, in order to cut off the desires that are afflictions, they live in seclusion. Through their blazing, diligent effort, up to their cultivation of right reflection, they cut off the desires that are afflictions and attain the stage of concentration free from desire. In this way, with right faith as support and guide, they can cross the flood of sense desire. How does heedfulness cross the great sea? They never relish that concentration, nor cling to it or rest in it; they focus their mind solely on realising the knowledge of the exhaustion of the outflows. Through this, the concentrated mind is pure, bright, upright, and pliant, and can enter direct realisation of the four noble truths, up to realising the exhaustion of the outflows for ever. In this way, with heedfulness as support and guide, they can cut off the two floods of existence bound to the form and formless realms, and cut off all the two floods of ignorance and views; so it is called crossing the great sea. How does vigour relinquish all suffering? Someone in training who has seen the path thinks: 'I should realise freedom from desire in the three realms and the exhaustion of all fetters for ever.' So they go into seclusion and abide there with courage and diligent effort, not letting the mind rest much in the entanglement of sensual desire. They also know as it really is the escape from the entanglements of sensual desire present now, purify their mind of the hindrance of sensual desire, and so can cut off the entanglements of sensual desire and the mental sorrow and pain born from them. As with the hindrance of sensual desire, so likewise through the hindrance of doubt. In this way, with vigour as support and guide, they can relinquish all suffering. How does wisdom attain purity? Having removed the five hindrances, which defile the mind and can obstruct ultimate nirvana, they rely on the preliminary stage and abide in it. With the uncontaminated knowledges of suffering, origination, cessation, and path attained before, they reflect on true suffering within suffering, and so on up to reflecting on the true path within the path, and so attain freedom from desire in all three realms without remainder and the exhaustion of the outflows for ever. In this way, with the wisdom attained before as support and guide, they can realise purity. Further, the meaning of what was said above will now be briefly set out. In this verse the Blessed One briefly shows ordinary beings who first become free from desire and afterwards are purified by direct realisation of the noble truths; and shows those in training who first directly realise the noble truths and are then purified by freedom from desire. It should be understood that this is the summary meaning here.

items.title: Topic Nine Continues: Crossing the Flood Without Drowsiness

items.zh: 誰超越暴流，晝夜無惛昧；於無攀無住，甚深無減劣？
items.en: Who crosses beyond the flood, free of dullness day and night, abiding in that grasping-free, lodging-free state — deep, complete, and undiminished?

items.zh: 圓滿眾尸羅、具慧、善安定、內思惟、繫念，能度極難度。
items.en: One who perfects the precepts entire, is endowed with wisdom and settled well in concentration, reflects inwardly with mindfulness fixed — such a one crosses what is hardest of all to cross.

items.zh: 諸欲想離染，亦超色界結，彼無攀無住、甚深無減劣。
items.en: Free of the stain of desire's every notion, surpassing also the fetters of the form realm — such a one abides grasping-free and lodging-free, deep, complete, and undiminished.

items.zh: 今此頌中，云何暴流？所謂四流。欲流、有流、見流、無明流。云何無攀無住？所謂諸愛永盡、離欲、寂滅、涅槃、及滅盡定。所以者何？所言攀者，諸煩惱纏；所言住者，煩惱隨眠。於彼處所二種俱無，是故說言無攀無住。此謂涅槃無攀無住。又想名攀，受名為住。若於是處二種俱無，即說彼處無攀無住。如是顯示滅想受定無攀無住。今此義中，意取滅定。云何圓滿眾尸羅？謂善安住身語律儀，修治淨命。云何具慧？謂於苦聖諦如實了知，乃至於道聖諦亦復如是。云何善安定？謂遠離諸欲，乃至具足安住第四靜慮，或第一有三摩鉢底。云何內思惟？謂於二十二處數數觀察。言我今者，容飾改常，去俗形好，廣說如經。云何繫念？謂於二十二處數觀察時，依沙門想恒作恒轉，而現在前；由此因緣，為斷餘結，修四念住。云何能度極難度？謂一切結無餘斷故，能度最極難度有頂。彼非一切愚夫異生可能度故。云何於諸欲想而得離染？謂於下分諸結已斷已知。云何超於色界諸結？謂於色繫上分諸結已斷已知。云何於無攀無住甚深中無有減劣？謂於無色界或已離欲、或未離欲，已得非想非非想處。堪能有力入滅盡定。學與無學俱容有此，故不定言超無色結。復次，今當略辨上所說義。謂薄伽梵於此頌中，略顯能得最究竟道，及顯能證第一住道。當知是名此中略義。
items.en: In this verse, what are the floods? The four floods: the flood of sense desire, the flood of existence, the flood of views, and the flood of ignorance. What is being without hold and without lodging? It is the exhaustion of all craving, freedom from desire, cessation, nirvana, and the attainment of cessation. Why? 'Hold' means the entanglements of the afflictions; 'lodging' means the latent tendencies of the afflictions. Where both are absent, it is said to be without hold and without lodging. This means nirvana is without hold and without lodging. Again, perception is called hold and feeling is called lodging. Where both are absent, that place is said to be without hold and without lodging. This shows that the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling is without hold and without lodging. In the present meaning, the attainment of cessation is intended. What is being complete in all ethics? It is abiding well in the restraint of body and speech and cultivating pure livelihood. What is being complete in wisdom? It is knowing the noble truth of suffering as it really is, and likewise up to the noble truth of the path. What is being well concentrated? It is being free from sense desires and so on up to fully abiding in the fourth dhyāna, or in the first attainment of existence. What is inner reflection? It is examining the twenty-two points again and again: 'I have now changed my appearance and left behind lay attire and adornment', and so on, as explained at length in the sūtra. What is fixing mindfulness? It is that, when examining the twenty-two points repeatedly, the perception of being an ascetic is constantly practised, constantly active, and present; and for this reason, to cut off the remaining fetters, one cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness. How can one cross what is extremely hard to cross? Because all fetters are cut off without remainder, one can cross the peak of existence, which is the hardest of all to cross; it cannot be crossed by foolish ordinary beings. How does one become free from defilement in perceptions of sense desire? By having cut off and fully known the lower fetters. How does one surpass the fetters of the form realm? By having cut off and fully known the higher fetters bound to form. How is one undiminished in the depth of being without hold and without lodging? It means that, whether or not one is already free from desire for the formless realm, one has attained the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception and has the capacity and strength to enter the attainment of cessation. Both those in training and those beyond training may have this, so it does not say definitely that one surpasses the formless fetters. Further, the meaning of what was said above will now be briefly set out. In this verse the Blessed One briefly shows the path by which the most ultimate is attained, and shows the path by which the foremost abiding is realised. It should be understood that this is the summary meaning here.

blocks.text: Two verse dialogues on crossing the flood. **Most of the explanations are missing from Ru-Yi's translation** (0376a02–b04 and 0376b11–c10); the English column gives our own translation, and the commentary summarises them.
"Right faith crosses the flood. Heedfulness crosses the great sea. Vigour relinquishes all suffering. Wisdom attains purity."

items: **Faith.** Hearing the Dharma, one gains faith and wishes to cut both desire as object and desire as affliction. One goes forth, practises in solitude, and reaches a concentration free of sense desire. Faith is the support and guide for crossing the flood of desire.

**Heedfulness.** One never relishes that concentration (Master Cháng Bǎi: it is a means, not the goal) and directs the mind only to the knowledge of the corruptions' end. With a pure, upright mind one realises the four truths, crossing the floods of existence, ignorance, and views: "the great sea".
**Vigour.** A trainee who has "seen the track" resolves to be free of all three realms, and abandons the five hindrances one by one, together with the sorrow they cause.
**Wisdom.** Relying on the preparatory stage of the first dhyāna (未至定), one reflects on suffering as suffering, and so on to the path as path, and all corruptions end.
**In brief:** the verse shows two routes: an ordinary being who first frees himself from desire and then sees the truths; and a trainee who first sees the truths and then becomes free of desire.

blocks.text: Who crosses, free of dullness day and night, abiding in that grasping-free (無攀), lodging-free (無住) state? One perfect in precepts, wise, settled in concentration, reflecting inwardly with mindfulness fixed.

items: The **floods** are four: desire, existence, views, ignorance.

"**Grasping**" is affliction in manifestation; "**lodging**" is its latent tendency. Where both are absent, that is nirvāṇa. Alternatively, grasping is perception and lodging is feeling; where both are absent, that is the **attainment of cessation** (滅盡定), which is meant here. Master Cháng Bǎi: "the foremost abiding".
**Inward reflection** means examining oneself repeatedly on the twenty-two points a renunciant should reflect on ("I have changed my appearance, left the ways of the world…").
Crossing "what is hardest to cross" is passing beyond the peak of existence.

The verse does not say the formless fetters are surpassed, because both trainees and those beyond training may enter cessation. Master Cháng Bǎi: a non-returner may not yet be free of formless-realm desire.

quiz.q: In answering the four questions, by what does the Buddha say one crosses the flood, crosses the sea, relinquishes suffering, and attains purity?
options: right faith crosses the flood, heedfulness crosses the sea, vigour relinquishes suffering, wisdom attains purity
quiz.why: The answer verse: right faith crosses the flood; heedfulness crosses the great sea; vigour relinquishes all suffering; wisdom attains purity.

quiz.q: "無逸" is rendered "heedlessness-free diligence," and the note's heading even writes "heedlessness." How does Master Cháng Bǎi gloss it?
options: being without heedlessness one crosses the sea of birth and death — heedfulness; the heading reverses it
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: being without heedlessness, one crosses the great sea of birth and death. 無逸 means heedfulness; the §10 heading "faith, heedlessness, diligence, and wisdom" says the opposite.

quiz.q: How, per Master Cháng Bǎi, does the heedful practitioner regard meditative concentration?
options: concentration is a means, not the goal — one does not cling to it
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: concentration is a means, not the ultimate; one does not cling firmly to it. Relying on it to realise the four truths is what crosses the sea of birth and death.

quiz.q: Which attainment do the two masters identify as the "grasping-free, lodging-free" state?
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: only one attainment can do this, called in Buddhism the foremost abiding — cessation-attainment. Venerable Miào Jìng: the "path of the foremost abiding" means cessation-attainment.

quiz.q: Who can attain cessation-attainment, and how does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "undiminished"?
options: non-returners can attain it, arhats more fully, and great bodhisattvas perfect it
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: non-returners can attain it, but arhats more completely, and only great bodhisattvas perfect the state of cessation-attainment. He also says it is open to both non-returners and arhats.

quiz.q: The third verse says only "surpassing the fetters of the form realm." Why not the formless realm too, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: the formless realm does not exist
because non-returners have not fully severed formless-realm innate self-clinging and desire
lack of space in the verse
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: because non-returners have not yet fully severed the innate self-clinging of the formless realm and are not yet free of formless-realm desire, the verse does not say they surpass the formless fetters.
